# 2 Samuel Chapter 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 193v–193r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_021_page_001.jpg, 2SA_021_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. And David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, "It is because of Saul and his bloodstained house, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

**2** So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them — now the Gibeonites were not of the sons of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the sons of Israel had sworn an oath to them, but Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah.

**3** And David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?"

**4** The Gibeonites said to him, "It is not a matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house, nor is it for us to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "Tell me what you want, and I will do it for you."

**5** They said to the king, "The man who consumed us and who plotted against us, so that we were destroyed from remaining anywhere in the territory of Israel —

**6** let seven of his sons be given to us, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD." And the king said, "I will give them."

**7** But the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

**8** So the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul — Armoni and Mephibosheth — and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

**9** And he gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain before the LORD. All seven fell together; they were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

**10** Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until rain poured upon them from heaven. She did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest upon them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

**11** And it was told to David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

**12** So David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them on the day the Philistines struck down Saul on Gilboa.

**13** And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.

**14** And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin, in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father. And they did all that the king commanded. And after this God was entreated for the land.

**15** Now the Philistines had war again with Israel. And David went down with his servants, and they fought against the Philistines. And David grew weary.

**16** And Ishbi-benob, who was among the descendants of the giant — the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and who was armed with new armor — intended to strike down David.

**17** But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid and struck the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, "You shall not go out with us to battle again, lest you extinguish the lamp of Israel."

**18** After this there was again war with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was among the descendants of the giant.

**19** And there was again war with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

**20** And there was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot — twenty-four in number — and he also was descended from the giant.

**21** And when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimei, David's brother, struck him down.

**22** These four were descended from the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

The three translators agree on the narrative structure: the Gibeonite blood-guilt episode (vv.1–14), followed by four Philistine giant encounters (vv.15–22). Key textual difficulties — the Michal/Merab question (v.8), the Elhanan/Goliath contradiction (v.19), and the nature of the execution verb *yaqa'* (v.6) — are noted by all three translators and preserved without harmonization. The Rizpah episode (v.10) is recognized by all as one of the most powerful passages in 2 Samuel.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "house of blood" vs. "bloodstained house"
- **EMET:** "the-house of-the-bloods [ha-damim]"
- **LOGOS:** "his house of blood"
- **PNEUMA:** "his bloodstained house"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his bloodstained house." PNEUMA's rendering best captures the force of the plural *damim* while remaining natural. LOGOS's "house of blood" is acceptable but less vivid.

### V.4 — "What do you say?" vs. "What are you saying?" vs. "Tell me what you want"
- **EMET:** "What [are]-you saying?"
- **LOGOS:** "What do you say?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Tell me what you want"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Tell me what you want, and I will do it for you." Combines PNEUMA's directness with the full clause from the Hebrew.

### V.6 — "hang" vs. execution terminology
- **EMET:** "we-will-hang-them [hoqa'anum]"
- **LOGOS:** "we will hang them"
- **PNEUMA:** "we will hang them"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "we will hang them." All three agree. The verb *yaqa'* likely refers to public exposure of the body, but "hang" is the conventional English rendering.

### V.9 — "fell together" vs. "died together"
- **EMET:** "fell [the]-seven of-them together"
- **LOGOS:** "the seven of them fell together"
- **PNEUMA:** "All seven died together"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "All seven fell together." Combines PNEUMA's "all seven" with the more literal "fell" from EMET/LOGOS, since *naflu* means "fell."

### V.10 — "water was poured" vs. "rain fell" vs. "rains came pouring down"
- **EMET:** "water was-poured upon-them from the-heavens"
- **LOGOS:** "rain fell upon them from heaven"
- **PNEUMA:** "the rains came pouring down from the sky"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "rain poured upon them from heaven." Preserves the verb *nittakh* ("was poured") from EMET while using natural English from LOGOS.

### V.16 — "said to strike" vs. "said he would strike" vs. "was about to kill"
- **EMET:** "he-said to-strike David"
- **LOGOS:** "said he would strike down David"
- **PNEUMA:** "He was about to kill David"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "intended to strike down David." LOGOS's phrasing with the more precise "intended" rather than the literal "said."

### V.17 — "helped him" vs. "came to his aid" vs. "rushed in"
- **EMET:** "helped-him Avishai"
- **LOGOS:** "Abishai came to his aid"
- **PNEUMA:** "Abishai rushed in"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Abishai came to his aid" — follows LOGOS. PNEUMA's "rushed in" adds urgency not in the Hebrew *'azar*.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
